analysis: What changed vs the 6 AM brief: the slide is now live in the cash session — Dow -0.1%, S&P -0.5%, Nasdaq -1.2% in the first 30 minutes, putting a seventh straight down day in sight and the worst week since early last year. Anthropic opened at $89.86 and was trading ~$92 at 9:54 AM ET, down ~5% on the day but off its lows — the $83 IPO price has not been tested yet, which is a small improvement on the premarket fear. Nvidia is the new pressure point: down 4% early to ~$140, below the $145.71 52-week low, after Thursday's California AG subpoena and more ARK selling. But the tape is not uniformly red: Alphabet is +2% and Apple +0.4% early, a split inside the Mag 7 that premarket futures didn't show. The 10-year yield has slipped back under 5% (~4.97%) and the VIX is holding ~30.9, not spiking further — the fear gauge is elevated but stable so far. Signal vs noise: the seventh-day slide, NVDA breaking its 52-week low, and the near-certain December hike are signal; the exact early-session Mag 7 prints and the ANT intraday wiggle are noise until the close confirms them. The open now hinges on whether ANT holds above $83, whether the S&P holds Thursday's 7,173.63 intraday low, and whether Michigan sentiment at 10 AM ET gives the tape any reason to stabilize into monthly options expiration.

headlines.headline: Selloff extends into a seventh day in the cash session: Dow -0.1%, S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq Composite -1.2% in the first 30 minutes (Barron's live coverage, ~6:45 AM PT). The S&P broke below 7,300 support on Thursday and is on pace for its seventh straight down day; the indexes are on track for their worst week since early last year.
headlines.why_it_matters: The premarket slide survived the open rather than fading — sellers are pressing, not covering, and there has been no new negative tech news overnight to explain it.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) opened at $89.86 and was trading ~$92.06 at 9:54 AM ET, down ~5.3% from Thursday's $97.17 close (Finnhub). It is off its $87.26 intraday low and still above the $83 IPO price, after closing day one 17% above the offer but 13% below its $111.50 open.
headlines.why_it_matters: Day two is holding above the $83 offer so far — a break of $83 hardens the 'IPO as top' read, while holding it gives the AI trade a floor to argue from.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) down 4% early to ~$140.14, below its $145.71 52-week low (Agyata/Yahoo, 14:40 UTC). Fresh overhang: California AG Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena Thursday over whether Nvidia chips reached China in violation of export controls and whether investors were misled; Cathie Wood's ARK sold another 33,430 shares Thursday after selling 543,092 on Nov 16; Moody's cut its credit outlook to Stable. The stock is ~38% below its October peak, with ~$669B of market value lost in six sessions.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI bellwether keeps leading down — succession uncertainty plus a live state probe is a double overhang, and the record Q3 (EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B vs $109.28B, Q4 guide $130B) is not stopping it.

headlines.headline: Mag 7 split in the early session: Alphabet +2.0% and Apple +0.4% green; Meta -2.2%, Tesla -1.7%, Amazon -1.0%, Microsoft -0.7% (Agyata/Yahoo, 14:40 UTC). Thursday all seven fell, with Amazon -3.9% and Alphabet -3.5% leading the losses.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tape is not uniformly red — Alphabet and Apple holding green while chips and Meta slide is the first divergence inside the mega-cap complex this week.

headlines.headline: Apple is working on an AI agent that can operate a computer — apps, browsing and coding — Bloomberg reported, based on a new job listing; TechCrunch reported the same listing. Apple has announced nothing. AAPL was +0.5% premarket and is +0.4% early, the most resilient Mag 7 name this week (-0.9% Thursday, ~2% below its 52-week high).
headlines.why_it_matters: A concrete AI-agent effort is the kind of catalyst Apple watchers have been waiting for — but it rests on a job listing, not an announcement, so treat it as a signal, not a product.

headlines.headline: Tesla (TSLA) upgraded by HSBC from Reduce to Hold, with the price target raised to $359 from $157 (MarketBeat, Nov 20). TSLA is -1.7% early to ~$368 after falling 2.4% Thursday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A big target raise on a red tape is a small counterweight — the upgrade is being overwhelmed by the broad AI selloff, so it matters more as a sentiment marker than a price driver today.

headlines.headline: Intuit (INTU) still the morning's big single-name story: down ~10% after agreeing to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for ~$3.68B — about one-third of the ~$12B it paid in 2021 — and cutting full-year revenue guidance despite beating on the top and bottom lines (Q1 revenue $4.35B, +12%; adjusted EPS $2.91). Deal is $3.31B cash plus $368M in Bending Spoons stock, expected to close early 2027; proceeds earmarked for buybacks.
headlines.why_it_matters: A guidance cut plus a fire-sale exit from a big acquisition is being punished hard — the market is also reading it as AI disruption hitting conventional software.

headlines.headline: December hike pricing sits near certainty (~97-99% for a 25bp hike), with Philly Fed President Anna Paulson saying Thursday the Fed will need to raise again because inflation is too high. Fed speakers today: Waller spoke at 8:25 AM ET; Cook speaks at 12:15 PM ET. The 10-year Treasury yield has slipped back under 5% to ~4.97%, down ~8 bps from Thursday's 5.05% close.
headlines.why_it_matters: A December hike is near-certain in market pricing — with no jobs report today, Fed speakers and Michigan sentiment are the only levers that can move it before the meeting.

headlines.headline: Retail earnings still moving: BJ's Wholesale -5% to -6% despite better-than-expected results this morning; Ross Stores -6%; Gap +3% to +3.5% after beating and trimming its outlook; Elastic -3% (Investopedia/IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is still discriminating on the consumer — Gap is rewarded, BJ's and Ross are sold even on decent numbers — but the tape's direction is overwhelming the stock-picking.
